queer_characters.name: Paul Korner
queer_characters.notes: A violinist openly portrayed as a gay man who falls in love with a male student; his suicide after blackmail and social rejection is framed by the filmmakers as an indictment of Paragraph 175 rather than punishment, and the film includes educational speeches presenting orientation as a natural variation.

contributor_notes: 1919 German silent film, one of the first sympathetic gay portrayals in cinema, co-written and partially funded by sexologist Magnus Hirschfeld as a polemic against Paragraph 175. The tragic-queer/bury-your-gays tropes are present (Korner's suicide) but the source text stresses this is framed as social critique, not punitive — hence rep_quality 'historical-context'. Hirschfeld's own identity is not stated in the source text, so he is not tagged as a queer creator; a maintainer may verify. No subtitle/audio info given. Content includes flashbacks depicting attempts to change orientation (conversion-therapy) and parental rejection.
